heading: Gibraltar goods transaction-tax transition v0.8
text: > **Source-cited draft.** Professional review is pending. Figures are limited to the periods and assumptions below. This Guide prepares working papers; it is not authority to file or pay.

heading: Scope
text: Prepare an evidence-led review of goods imports, local production and the 2026 transaction-tax transition. This is a transition research draft, not a customs declaration or an exhaustive commodity-rate catalogue.

heading: Scope
text: Sources were accessed on 22 October 2026. A dated rate table controls its stated period; an undated guidance page does not prove that all later amendments have been incorporated.

heading: Enacted scope and commencement
text: Section 98 charges goods **produced in Gibraltar or imported into Gibraltar**, subject to exemptions and exclusions. The consolidation's commencement table records the remaining provisions commencing on 15 July 2026 under LN 2026/148. Use the enacted goods charge rather than the earlier March press explanation as the scope authority. This Guide does not establish a general retail VAT or a service-tax regime. [Act, commencement table and section 98](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/treaty-on-gibraltar/2026-11/2026-11(15-07-26).pdf).

heading: Enacted scope and commencement
text: Under section 100, the declarant or person on whose behalf entry is declared is liable. Others involved in irregular entry are also liable; for Gibraltar production, the producer is liable. Identify the liable person before allocating the charge to a customer or an intermediary. [Section 100](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/treaty-on-gibraltar/2026-11/2026-11(15-07-26).pdf).

heading: Identify the chargeable event
text: Schedule 2 paragraph 1 charges and collects tax at these events:

heading: Identify the chargeable event
text:
- Goods in Union free circulation transported under the special Gibraltar transit procedure: presentation to customs.
- Goods from outside the customs union transported under the relevant special transit procedure: presentation to customs.
- Within the special fiscal/customs procedures: Union goods put on the Gibraltar market, or a customs debt arising for non-Union goods.
- Gibraltar-produced goods leaving the production site.
- Discovery of irregular entry.
- Travellers' non-commercial goods above the applicable quantitative thresholds: declaration or completion of checks.

heading: Identify the chargeable event
text: For local production, leaving includes physical dispatch regardless of destination or purpose **and transfer of the right to dispose as owner even if the goods remain at the facility**. Record both dates; do not wait for physical delivery where ownership-disposal rights have already transferred. The treaty Annex 23 traveller thresholds and Annexes 19/21 procedures need separate verification for the actual movement. [Schedule 2, paragraph 1, printed pages 103–104](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/treaty-on-gibraltar/2026-11/2026-11(15-07-26).pdf).

heading: Calculate the taxable amount
text: For imports, begin with customs value. Add import taxes, duties, levies and other charges, including excise but excluding transaction tax itself, and incidental costs such as commission, packing, transport and insurance, **only insofar as not already included**. Reconcile invoices and the customs valuation to prevent duplicate freight or insurance. [Schedule 2, paragraph 2(1)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/treaty-on-gibraltar/2026-11/2026-11(15-07-26).pdf).

heading: Calculate the taxable amount
text: For Gibraltar production, use open-market value when the goods leave production: the amount payable at the same marketing stage in fair competition to an arm's-length Gibraltar supplier. If no comparable supply can be identified, the statutory floor is purchase price of those or similar goods, or, absent a purchase price, cost price at that time. A cost floor is not an unconditional permission to ignore an identifiable comparable market value. [Paragraph 2(2)–(4)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/treaty-on-gibraltar/2026-11/2026-11(15-07-26).pdf).

heading: Rate selection and period controls
text: The treaty date rule is now reconciled. Article 336(4) treats references in the agreement to entry into force as references to provisional application once provisional application begins. The Council register records **15 July 2026**. Domestic sections 6 and 10 give the treaty effect from the Implementation Date and require domestic law to operate consistently with it. Annex 24, Part II, paragraph 3(a), supplies the year-one/year-two/year-three rate sequence; domestic Schedule 2 paragraph 3 expresses the first two periods as 12 and 24 months. [Treaty, Articles 248 and 336](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6a56149a6d6d5c7e2845c8d1/MS_9.2026_Agreement_Gibraltar_UK_EU_EAEC_v1of2.pdf); [Annex 24](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6a56149a9e63154454413620/MS_9.2026_Agreement_Gibraltar_UK_EU_EAEC_v2of2.pdf); [domestic sections 6, 10 and Schedule 2](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/treaty-on-gibraltar/2026-11/2026-11(15-07-26).pdf).

heading: Rate selection and period controls
text: The resulting calendar, derived from those provisions, is:

heading: Rate selection and period controls
text:
| Period under the baseline enactment | Standard rate |
|---|---|
| 15 July 2026–14 July 2027 | 15% |
| 15 July 2027–14 July 2028 | 16% |
| From 15 July 2028 | 17% or the lowest Member State standard rate then applicable, as provided by the legislation |

heading: Rate selection and period controls
text: This calendar is a derivation from the current enactment and treaty, not a promise that future legislation stays unchanged. Section 99 permits amendments and contains conditions and an exception for consultative-body recommendations. Annex 24 also provides for recommendations affecting goods/categories. Check amendments and applicable category rates on the chargeable-event date. A later general ratification date does not restart the treaty's elapsed provisional-application period. [Article 336(3)–(4)](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6a56149a6d6d5c7e2845c8d1/MS_9.2026_Agreement_Gibraltar_UK_EU_EAEC_v1of2.pdf); [Annex 24, Part II, paragraph 3(a)](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6a56149a9e63154454413620/MS_9.2026_Agreement_Gibraltar_UK_EU_EAEC_v2of2.pdf).

heading: Rate selection and period controls
text: **Date-boundary illustration:** assuming the baseline law remains unchanged and the goods are standard-rated, an established £1,000 taxable amount charged on 14 July 2027 produces £150; the same amount charged on 15 July 2027 produces £160. Use the statutory chargeable event, not the order date. This is a future-period illustration, not a verified future rate ruling.

heading: Rate selection and period controls
text: The schedule's 5% categories include agricultural inputs subject to capital-goods exclusions and the chemical pesticide/fertiliser time limit; live equines; specified plants/floricultural goods; children's clothing, footwear and car seats; bicycles including electric bicycles; defined art, collectors' items and antiques; and qualifying rescue/first-aid equipment supplied to public or eligible nonprofit bodies. Classification depends on the full statutory description, recipient and any incorporated EU definition. [Paragraph 3(2), printed page 105](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/treaty-on-gibraltar/2026-11/2026-11(15-07-26).pdf).

heading: Rate selection and period controls
text: The 0% categories cover specified foodstuffs excluding alcoholic beverages, water, qualifying pharmaceutical/hygiene products, medical/disability equipment, qualifying publications, and solar panels for the specified buildings. Publication exclusions include predominantly advertising, video or audible-music content. These are category summaries, not a commodity classification decision; retain the exact applicable row and evidence. A zero rate does not by itself remove declaration obligations. [Paragraph 3(3), printed pages 105–106](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/treaty-on-gibraltar/2026-11/2026-11(15-07-26).pdf).

heading: Recomputable examples
text: These are assumed classification/rate cases, not rulings on particular goods:

heading: Recomputable examples
text:
1. **Import:** customs value £10,000 already includes £400 freight. Separately chargeable excise £1,000 and packing £200 are not included. Taxable amount = £10,000 + £1,000 + £200 = **£11,200**. At an established 15% rate, tax = **£1,680**. Adding the £400 again would overstate tax by £60.
2. **Local production:** established comparable open-market value £8,000; production cost £6,000. At an established 15% rate, tax = **£1,200**, not £900. If disposal rights transfer before dispatch, leaving occurs on that transfer under paragraph 1(2)(b).
3. **No comparable supply:** no purchase price is available and evidenced cost price is £6,000. That establishes a floor of £6,000, not proof that any lower invoice price is acceptable. At 15%, tax on the floor is £900; confirm the final taxable valuation before using that amount.

heading: Recomputable examples
text: These checks recompute the stated assumptions; they do not determine commodity classification, valuation or rate eligibility.

heading: Recomputable examples
text:
```oa-check
name: Import valuation without duplicate freight
inputs:
  customs_value: 10000
  excise_not_included: 1000
  packing_not_included: 200
  freight_already_included: 400
  rate: 0.15
steps:
  - taxable_amount: customs_value + excise_not_included + packing_not_included
  - tax: taxable_amount * rate
  - duplicate_freight_overstatement: freight_already_included * rate
expected:
  taxable_amount: 11200
  tax: 1680
  duplicate_freight_overstatement: 60
```

heading: Recomputable examples
text:
```oa-check
name: Local production with comparable market value
inputs:
  comparable_value: 8000
  cost: 6000
  rate: 0.15
steps:
  - tax_on_comparable_value: comparable_value * rate
  - tax_on_cost: cost * rate
  - understatement_using_cost: tax_on_comparable_value - tax_on_cost
expected:
  tax_on_comparable_value: 1200
  tax_on_cost: 900
  understatement_using_cost: 300
```
4. **Rate sensitivity:** an independently established £1,000 taxable amount gives £150 at 15%, £50 at 5%, or £0 at 0%. The arithmetic does not prove eligibility for a reduced category.

heading: Exemptions and export refunds
text: Section 101 applies mandatory EU VAT exemptions by asking whether the goods would qualify if imported, supplied or acquired in the EU. A discretionary exemption requires the Committee approval and Minister's Gazette notice described there. It expressly exempts LNG imported and used for electricity production and electricity produced in Gibraltar. Do not treat all fuels or all energy equipment as exempt. [Section 101](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/treaty-on-gibraltar/2026-11/2026-11(15-07-26).pdf).

heading: Exemptions and export refunds
text: For commercial exports to the EU, section 102 requires proof satisfactory to the Collector that EU VAT was paid. For exports outside the customs union, it requires export through a designated customs post and notification to the Collector by that post. Goods consumed in Gibraltar do not qualify for refund. Obtain export and destination-tax evidence; this is not an automatic credit for every overseas sale. Refund forms, submission deadlines and operational processing remain unverified. [Section 102](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/treaty-on-gibraltar/2026-11/2026-11(15-07-26).pdf).

heading: Working-paper procedure
text: Record the goods, liable person, date/event, customs procedure and supporting documents. Establish exemption or rate classification; reconcile the valuation components; compute tax; match the declaration and payment evidence. Keep any export-refund claim and income-tax transition relief separate. Review bonded stock and other transitional procedures before using these rules for pre-commencement stock.

heading: Published customs declaration route
text: HM Customs' [Goods Transit Process, sections 2 and 4.2](https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/uploads/_PressOffice/Treaty%20Customs%20Guidance/Transit%20GN.pdf) describes these operational steps:

heading: Published customs declaration route
text:
- For home-use arrivals, present goods to Customs for NCTS arrival confirmation and controls, then submit an **IM4** in ASYCUDA, linking the consignment's movement reference number (MRN).
- Clearance produces an assessment; transaction tax is payable before release. The note permits up to **30 days' deferral in some cases** where goods are not immediately marketed, notably transit-shed stock. This is not a general payment extension.
- For exports of goods already marketed with transaction tax paid, section 4.2 calls for **EX1**, the original import invoice/MRN, and the relevant NCTS transit declaration. Spanish arrival confirmation supports proof of export.

heading: Published customs declaration route
text: That guidance does not replace section 102's destination-tax and export conditions. Section 4.2 retains a reference to “Section 6 (iv) (A) to (D)” that does not match this note's headings; the destination-treatment cross-reference needs clarification. No live declaration, deferment approval or refund claim has been tested. Retain the assessment, payment/release evidence and linked movement records.

heading: Transitional goods: distinguish movement, certificates and storage
text: Section 6 defines the Implementation Date to include provisional implementation unless the contrary is expressed or implied. The Council treaty register confirms provisional application from **15 July 2026**. Use that evidenced date when examining these domestic transition provisions; do not use the superseded expected April date found in early notices. [Act, section 6](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/treaty-on-gibraltar/2026-11/2026-11(15-07-26).pdf); [Council treaty register](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/documents/treaties-agreements/agreement/?docLanguage=en&id=2026009).

heading: Transitional goods: distinguish movement, certificates and storage
text: **Goods already moving:** section 130(2) disapplies the specified treaty title and Part 6 of the Act to movements that started before the Implementation Date and ended afterwards. The operator bears the burden of proving the earlier start with relevant documents. Section 130(5) ends that treatment two months after the Implementation Date. An order or invoice raised before implementation does not by itself prove that movement began then. [Section 130(1)–(5), printed pages 82–83](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/treaty-on-gibraltar/2026-11/2026-11(15-07-26).pdf).

heading: Transitional goods: distinguish movement, certificates and storage
text: **Earlier import-duty exemption certificates:** section 130(3) concerns certificates issued by the Chief Minister under the specified 2017 Tariff Regulations provision before implementation. It requires the government-to-EU transmission of certificates and relevant historical quantities and quantities commensurate with the projects. The relief is limited by Article 269(4). Section 130(6) limits duration to the shorter of the certificate's duration and three months from implementation. Retaining a certificate alone does not establish every condition; verify the treaty limitation and transmission evidence before claiming. [Section 130(3), (4), (6)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/treaty-on-gibraltar/2026-11/2026-11(15-07-26).pdf).

heading: Transitional goods: distinguish movement, certificates and storage
text: **Goods already lawfully marketed:** section 130(7) provides three months without the Article 256 requirements for goods lawfully placed on the market before implementation. The operator must prove prior placement and quantities. This provision refers to product requirements; do not turn it into a blanket transaction-tax exemption for every item of old stock. [Section 130(7)–(8)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/treaty-on-gibraltar/2026-11/2026-11(15-07-26).pdf).

heading: Transitional goods: distinguish movement, certificates and storage
text: **Special procedures and temporary storage:** section 131 preserves the pre-implementation legislation for goods already in the relevant procedure/storage, subject to different limits. A special procedure is protected only while not discharged and for no longer than two months from implementation. Temporary storage is protected only while it has not ended and no later than its legal time limit. The section does **not** itself state a universal 30-day storage period. Release for free circulation, discharge and re-export fall under the specified treaty title under section 131(3). Read the applicable procedure before treating stored goods as tax-free. [Section 131, printed pages 83–84](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/treaty-on-gibraltar/2026-11/2026-11(15-07-26).pdf).

heading: Transitional goods: distinguish movement, certificates and storage
text: **Evidence example:** on assumed authentic transport records, a consignment whose movement began on 14 July and ended on 20 July 2026 meets the before/after timing limb of section 130(2). A consignment first dispatched on 16 July fails that limb even if ordered on 1 July. For a qualifying certificate, if the evidenced remaining duration is one month, the shorter-of-one-and-three-months rule allows at most one month; the other conditions still apply. Do not extend either case merely because goods remain unsold.

heading: Transitional goods: distinguish movement, certificates and storage
text: These provisions establish separate routes, not interchangeable exemptions. Attach transport-start evidence, customs procedure records, certificates and quantities to the working paper. Exact time-limit computation, incorporated treaty conditions and any subsequent amendment must be checked for a boundary-date claim.

heading: Transitional business relief: eligibility
text: The enacted Transaction Tax (Deductions) Rules commenced on 23 September 2026. Rule 3 covers companies, partnerships, sole traders and other incorporated or unincorporated retail/wholesale traders certified by the Office of Fair Trading. It excludes trades principally selling food, beverages and household groceries, tobacco, wine or spirits, fuel, or vehicles. Obtain certification of the actual business; an ordinary business licence alone does not establish eligibility. [Rules 2–3](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2026s338/2026s338.pdf).

heading: Transitional business relief: eligibility
text: Rule 4 covers transaction-tax costs within 90 days beginning on the Implementation Date and measures the deduction by tax paid in that period. The official announcement identifies the initial window as **15 July–12 October 2026**. Do not substitute an invoice date for proof of tax payment. Rule 5 permits a further 90 days by Gazette notice following the specified independent committee advice and provides for advice on subsequent extensions. No extension notice has been verified for this Guide; post-12-October payments must remain outside its supported calculation unless that evidence is obtained. [Rules 4(1), 5](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2026s338/2026s338.pdf); [official period explanation](https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/press-releases/minister-arias-vasquez-publishes-transaction-tax-deductions-rules-2026-6922026-12358).

heading: Compute the deduction, separately from tax saved
text:
1. Establish eligible transaction tax **paid** in the supported period.
2. Calculate the import duty that would previously have applied in that same period. For imports subject to multiple historical rates, rule 4(2) requires a weighted average using broad goods categories and their proportions of total imports. Retain the categories, allocation basis, historical rates, customs declarations and purchase records. The Commissioner must be satisfied with the calculation and can require more evidence or withhold/adjust it.
3. Calculate the positive difference between transaction tax and counterfactual duty. If transaction tax is not higher, no deduction arises under rule 4(1).
4. Limit that amount to **50% of tax paid in the immediately preceding accounting period or year of assessment**. Use evidence of payment, not merely the assessed liability.
5. Apply eligibility, aid and other-support restrictions below. Deduct the permitted amount in computing assessable profits for the accounting period/year commencing on or after the Implementation Date; do not automatically put it into the period containing an import date. The announcement describes the first such period.

heading: Compute the deduction, separately from tax saved
text: This is a profit deduction. The deduction amount is not itself a tax credit, repayment or customs refund. [Rule 4(1)–(5)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2026s338/2026s338.pdf).

heading: Compute the deduction, separately from tax saved
text: **Mixed-import illustration:** assume an evidenced £100,000 historical duty base, with accepted value proportions of 60% at a historical 10% rate and 40% at 0%. The weighted rate is 60% × 10% + 40% × 0% = **6%**, giving counterfactual duty of **£6,000**. Eligible transaction tax actually paid is £15,000, so the difference is £9,000. If immediately preceding-period tax paid was £12,000, the cap is £6,000 and the provisional deduction is **min(£9,000, £6,000) = £6,000**, subject to all remaining conditions. Assuming sufficient taxable profits and an independently established 15% income-tax rate, the resulting tax reduction would be **£900**, not £6,000. The example does not establish any real commodity's historical rate, valuation or allocation basis.

heading: Compute the deduction, separately from tax saved
text:
```oa-check
name: Mixed imports deduction limited by prior tax paid
inputs:
  historical_base: 100000
  taxable_proportion: 0.60
  zero_rate_proportion: 0.40
  historical_rate: 0.10
  other_rate: 0
  transaction_tax_paid: 15000
  previous_period_tax_paid: 12000
  income_tax_rate: 0.15
steps:
  - weighted_rate: taxable_proportion * historical_rate + zero_rate_proportion * other_rate
  - historical_duty: historical_base * weighted_rate
  - positive_difference: max(0, transaction_tax_paid - historical_duty)
  - cap: previous_period_tax_paid * 0.50
  - deduction: min(positive_difference, cap)
  - assumed_tax_saving: deduction * income_tax_rate
expected:
  weighted_rate: 0.06
  historical_duty: 6000
  positive_difference: 9000
  cap: 6000
  deduction: 6000
  assumed_tax_saving: 900
```

heading: Compute the deduction, separately from tax saved
text: **Boundaries:** zero preceding-period tax paid gives a zero cap under the rule's formula. Equal transaction tax and counterfactual duty give no positive difference. These rules do not state a carry-forward entitlement for the excess above the cap; do not invent one. [Rule 4(1), (5)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2026s338/2026s338.pdf).

heading: Compliance, competing assistance and claim evidence
text: At the Implementation Date the claimant must meet all applicable filing and payment obligations for corporation/income tax, PAYE and social insurance. The Commissioner has discretion for a person who becomes compliant within 30 days after the Rules commenced, but only with a written application, supporting evidence and **written approval**. Catching up on filings alone does not establish approval. [Rule 4(6)–(8)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2026s338/2026s338.pdf).

heading: Compliance, competing assistance and claim evidence
text: Each claim requires OFT certification, payment documentation and the applicable weighted-average evidence. The Commissioner can adjust or disregard an inaccurate, overstated or non-genuine claim and must notify the determination in writing. Rule 4(11) excludes a person granted assistance under a scheme prescribed or published since the Implementation Date aimed at financially supporting modernisation of premises, processes/procedures, IT or staff training. Check assistance actually granted and the scheme's purpose and publication date; do not describe this only as a prohibition on double-claiming the same invoice. [Rule 4(9)–(11)](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2026s338/2026s338.pdf).

heading: Compliance, competing assistance and claim evidence
text: Rule 6 separately requires compliance with the applicable de minimis aid provisions. Declare and document de minimis and other state aid received during the **three years preceding the claim**. The Commissioner can reduce the deduction to the amount compatible with those provisions. This Guide does not establish the applicable monetary aid ceiling, aggregation rules or remaining headroom. [Rule 6](https://www.gibraltarlaws.gov.gi/uploads/legislations/income-tax/2026s338/2026s338.pdf).

heading: Compliance, competing assistance and claim evidence
text: **Outstanding verification:** verify any extension after 12 October and the applicable state-aid ceiling/aggregation; incorporated commodity definitions, customs procedures and traveller thresholds; remaining transitional-stock treaty conditions and boundary dates; declaration/payment deadlines, refund procedure and subsequent amendments. The charging provisions, statutory commencement table and valuation rules above have now been checked, but the operational transition is not fully verified.

heading: Self-checks and output
text:
- Retain the relevant source version, the applicable period and the facts establishing scope.
- Reconcile every input to the client's records; keep estimates separate from actual amounts.
- Recompute the example and boundary cases before applying the method.
- Record exclusions and unresolved points explicitly. Do not convert a missing source into an exemption.
- Deliver a calculation, evidence list, filing calendar and reviewer questions. Record the exact revision reviewed.
